title: Ordinary etale projective bundle and Chern identities over Noetherian bases
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme on which a prime $\ell$ is invertible, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Use ordinary small-etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and roots-of-unity twists [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. A vector bundle means a finite locally free module [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. For a rank-$r>0$ vector bundle $F$, let $p:P=\operatorname{Proj}_X(\operatorname{Sym}F)\to X$ be the projective bundle of line quotients [def-nagata-relative-proj], and put $\xi=c_1(\mathcal O_P(1))$, where $c_1$ is the Kummer boundary of the frame torsor [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. Then
$$(1,\xi,\ldots,\xi^{r-1}):\bigoplus_{a=0}^{r-1}\Lambda_X(-a)[-2a]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*\Lambda_P.$$
There are unique classes $c_i(F)\in H^{2i}(X,\Lambda(i))$ satisfying $c_0(F)=1$, $c_i(F)=0$ for $i>r$, and
$$\xi^r-p^*c_1(F)\xi^{r-1}+\cdots+(-1)^rp^*c_r(F)=0.$$
For rank zero set $c_0=1$ and $c_i=0$ for $i>0$. They agree with the Kummer first Chern class for lines, commute with pullback, and satisfy $c_t(F)=c_t(F')c_t(F'')$ for every short exact sequence $0\to F'\to F\to F''\to0$, where $c_t(F)=\sum_i c_i(F)t^i$. Moreover $c_i(F^\vee)=(-1)^ic_i(F)$. The projective bundle decomposition and all these classes commute with reduction $\mathbf Z/\ell^N\to\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ for $N\geq n$, using $u\mapsto u^{\ell^{N-n}}$ on roots of unity. The displayed cup products are the derived-tensor products on ordinary etale cohomology. No regularity or field-of-definition hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Expose XVI, Theorems 1.2 and 1.3, Propositions 1.4 and 1.7; coefficient compatibility of the Kummer construction and the uniquely determined projective-bundle coefficients.

proof.text: Use the Kummer sequence [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. The relative torsor construction [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology], with closed support all of $X$, sends a line bundle's frame torsor to its ordinary $c_1$. The additivity and dual identities of [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus] at full support give $c_1(L\otimes M)=c_1(L)+c_1(M)$, $c_1(L^\vee)=-c_1(L)$ and $c_1(\mathcal O)=0$. Naturality of relative connecting maps gives pullback naturality. Twists are locally free of rank one and pull back canonically by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Thus even-degree twisted classes commute, and their powers and all pullbacks below are the indicated derived-tensor cup products. The quotient-projective geometry, its properness, and its tautological base change are [lem-pur-projective-bundle-tautological-geometry]; no cohomological claim from the finite-field purity setting is used.

source.place: Definition 1.1 and the paragraph following it; Theorem 1.2, setup

proof.text: Form $\Phi_F$ as the sum of the adjoints of $\xi^a:\Lambda_P(-a)[-2a]\to\Lambda_P$. The ringed-topos derived adjunction and monoidal pullback are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Apply [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] to the proper $p$ and a geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$. Its torsion hypothesis holds for $\Lambda_P$. The canonical exchange identifies the stalk target with $R\Gamma(\mathbf P^{r-1}_\Omega,\Lambda)$. The module comparison [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-direct-image-comparison] permits this use of the abelian base-change theorem. By Step 1, each component is the same power of the geometric Kummer hyperplane class. The calculation [lem-per-geometric-projective-space-hyperplane-cohomology] says it is an isomorphism on every cohomology stalk. Exactness of a geometric-point inverse image gives stalks of cohomology sheaves. Now [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology] prove that $\Phi_F$ is an isomorphism. Both sides lie in $D^+$; their inclusion in the ordinary derived category gives the asserted map there.

Apply $\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda_X(-r)[-2r],-)$ to $\Phi_F$. The derived adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] and the invertible-twist evaluations [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] identify the resulting isomorphism with
$$\bigoplus_{a=0}^{r-1}H^{2(r-a)}(X,\Lambda(r-a))\longrightarrow H^{2r}(P,\Lambda(r)),\quad(b_a)_a\longmapsto\sum_a p^*b_a\xi^a.$$
Write $\xi^r=\sum_{i=1}^r(-1)^{i+1}p^*c_i(F)\xi^{r-i}$ using its unique coordinates. Set $c_0=1$ and $c_i=0$ for $i>r$. This proves existence and uniqueness without choosing an object from an undetermined existence assertion. For rank one, $P(F)=X$ and $\mathcal O(1)=F$ by [lem-pur-projective-bundle-tautological-geometry], so the relation reads $\xi=c_1(F)$. For rank zero use the stated convention.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 1.3, construction from the monic relation

proof.text: For a morphism $g:X'\to X$ between bases in the statement, tautological geometry identifies $P(g^*F)$ and its quotient line with the pullback. Pull back the monic relation; Step 1 identifies $g^*\xi$ with its new Kummer class. Uniqueness in Step 3 gives $g^*c_i(F)=c_i(g^*F)$. The same adjunction construction of each component, together with the canonical proper exchange of [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below], identifies $g^*\Phi_F$ with $\Phi_{g^*F}$. These are the canonical maps, rather than isomorphisms selected separately. Bundle isomorphisms give the same conclusion by the quotient construction.

Suppose $F=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r L_i$. The quotient description [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] gives $p^*F\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O(1)$. Let $H_i$ be the zero locus of its $i$th component $p^*L_i\to\mathcal O(1)$. Off $H_i$ that component trivializes $M_i=\mathcal O(1)\otimes p^*L_i^\vee$. Thus [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] lifts $c_1(M_i)=\xi-p^*c_1(L_i)$ to a supported Kummer class $x_i\in H^2_{H_i}(P,\Lambda(1))$. The supported product in [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus] puts $\prod_i x_i$ in support $\bigcap_i H_i$. This intersection is empty: at every point the components of a surjection onto a free rank-one module generate its unit ideal, so they cannot all vanish in the residue field. Cohomology with empty support is zero, since its defining left exact functor is zero [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections]. Forgetting support gives $\prod_i(\xi-p^*c_1(L_i))=0$. Coefficient uniqueness in Step 3 gives $c_t(F)=\prod_i(1+c_1(L_i)t)$. For $r=1$ the sole zero locus is empty; for $r=0$ the polynomial identity is the empty product convention.

source.place: Lemma 1.6, hyperplanes with empty common intersection

proof.text: The complete flag construction [def-pur-complete-flag-bundle] is an iterated quotient-projective bundle with a filtration by line quotients. At each projection $q$ the $a=0$ summand in Step 2 is the adjunction unit $\Lambda\to Rq_*\Lambda$ and has a retraction, namely the zero-coordinate projection of $\Phi^{-1}$. Applying $\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda(-b)[-v],-)$, the derived adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] and the twist identifications of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] show that pullback on $H^v(-,\Lambda(b))$ is injective. Iterating gives injectivity for the flag projection. All stages remain Noetherian, being covered by finitely many finite-type projective charts over a Noetherian base. Next, for every extension of vector bundles, [lem-per-vector-extension-splitting-cohomology] gives a Noetherian splitting scheme on which the extension is split and pullback on these groups is an isomorphism. Thus a finite tower of these flag and splitting maps detects equality in every twisted degree.

source.place: Propositions 1.4 and 1.5, the two splitting principles

proof.text: For $0\to F'\to F\to F''\to0$, first take its splitting scheme from Step 6. Then take a complete flag bundle for each of $F'$ and $F''$, successively pulling all bundles to the new base. Split the successive extensions in each universal filtration, working from its bottom line upwards. Explicitly, if the rank-$j-1$ term has already become $\bigoplus_{i<j}L_i$, apply the splitting-scheme node to $0\to F_{j-1}\to F_j\to L_j\to0$; its universal section identifies $F_j$ with $F_{j-1}\oplus L_j$. This terminates after their finite ranks. On the final base both $F'$ and $F''$ are sums of lines and $F=F'\oplus F''$. Step 5 expresses their Chern polynomials as products of the corresponding line factors, so the product for $F$ is their product. Step 4 identifies all these classes with pullbacks of the original ones; the composite pullback is injective degree by degree by Step 6. Therefore $c_t(F)=c_t(F')c_t(F'')$ on $X$. A zero-rank term is the zero module and contributes the empty product $1$. No Zariski-local detection of global cohomology is assumed.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 1.3 after Proposition 1.5, reduction to Lemma 1.6

proof.text: Apply the flag and splitting tower of Step 6 to a single $F$. On its final base $F=\bigoplus_i L_i$ and $F^\vee=\bigoplus_i L_i^\vee$. Step 1 changes each root $x_i=c_1(L_i)$ to $-x_i$ upon dualizing. Step 5 therefore gives $c_t(F^\vee)=\prod_i(1-x_it)=c_{-t}(F)$ there. Pullback commutes with finite locally free duals: in a local frame it is the identity on the dual basis and hence agrees on overlaps. By Step 4 and injectivity of the composite pullback, the equality descends to $X$, so its coefficient of $t^i$ is $c_i(F^\vee)=(-1)^ic_i(F)$. For rank zero this is $1=1$ in degree zero and $0=0$ in positive degrees.

For $M=\ell^N$, $m=\ell^n$ and $d=M/m$, the two Kummer sequences have a commuting map: on their left terms it is $\mu_M\to\mu_m$, $u\mapsto u^d$; on the middle $\mathbf G_m$ it is $z\mapsto z^d$; on the right $\mathbf G_m$ it is the identity, since $(z^d)^m=z^M$. Naturality of the connecting maps in [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] sends the Kummer class of each frame torsor to the class of that same torsor. The twist comparison is exactly [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], with tensor powers and dual evaluations for negative twists. Coefficient compatibility of products is [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus]. Hence each component $\xi_N^a$ maps to $\xi_n^a$ and the projective-bundle maps commute with the canonical coefficient comparison. One may check this square after restriction of scalars to abelian sheaves; no assertion that reduction is flat is used. If derived scalar extension is used instead, the canonical comparison $\Lambda_n\otimes^L_{\Lambda_N}Rp_*\Lambda_N\to Rp_*\Lambda_n$ is an isomorphism here: composing it with the scalar extension of $\Phi_{F,N}$ gives $\Phi_{F,n}$ under the Tate-line identifications, and both decomposition maps are isomorphisms. Finally reduce the monic relation of Step 3 coefficientwise; uniqueness at level $n$ gives the reduction of every $c_i(F)$. This also preserves the rank-zero convention.

I checked it against Riou, Exposé XVI (Travaux de Gabber pp. 225-228: Def 1.1, Thm 1.2/1.3, Props 1.4/1.5, Lemma 1.6, Prop 1.7) and Milne LEC Thm 23.2. Signs match Riou: xi^r - c1 xi^{r-1} + ... = 0, and the product of (xi - c1(L_i)) is 0. Step 2: proper base change at geometric points, where Omega is algebraically closed by def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions; module/abelian comparison; stalk-conservative and D+ detector. Step 5: the components of p*F onto O(1) cannot all vanish at a point, so the hyperplanes have empty intersection, and Gamma with empty support is 0. Steps 6-7: flag-unit retraction plus splitting schemes give an explicit terminating tower that detects equality. Step 9: I checked the Kummer map of sequences (u^d, z^d, id) and the m|m' twist clause. Two new nodes. (1) The geometric P^m hyperplane cohomology is true: checked m=0, char 0, both sign conventions. It is not a duplicate of thm-pur-projective-bundle-formula (pro-etale, finite-field base) or of the P^1 nodes. (2) The vector-extension splitting scheme (Riou Prop 1.5) is true: checked a=0 or b=0 and a nonsplit extension. No node gives general-base Z/l^n homotopy invariance. Neither node restates an item clause. No SGA in any source, no cycle, and proof_deps equals the union of uses. Batch 5: closure from both targets with versus without the item's proof differs only by the two new per nodes. lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry (pure Proj geometry) and thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below (proper base change, outside both assumptions) are both already in the base closure, so I accept them.
